headline: Record inflows and margin expansion drive a profit swing
summary_short: Invesco's ending AUM reached $2.47 trillion (+14.4% q/q) on record net long-term inflows of $45.1B, and net income attributable to Invesco Ltd. swung to $345.3M ($0.76 diluted EPS) from a $12.5M loss a year ago as adjusted operating margin expanded to 37.5% (+3ppt q/q).
summary_long: Revenue rose 20.5% y/y to $1,825.6M on higher average AUM and QQQ's fee contribution following its Q4 2025 ETF conversion, while service and distribution fees fell as QQQ's pass-through revenue was eliminated. Operating margin expanded to 19.9% GAAP (37.5% adjusted, +3ppt q/q) as expenses held flat sequentially against 5% higher net revenues. Net income attributable to Invesco Ltd. was $345.3M, swinging from a $12.5M loss a year earlier that included a $159.3M preferred-share repurchase cost; diluted EPS was $0.76. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.71, up 24.6% q/q. The company cut net debt by more than $450M to $708.6M, raised share buybacks to $50M, and declared a $0.215 common dividend. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Market gains of $256.8B and $45.1B of net long-term inflows drove the AUM increase, led by ETFs and Index, QQQ, and the China JV; the Canadian fund-business sale reduced AUM by $11.0B.
Retail inflows of $47.3B outweighed institutional outflows of $2.2B; ETFs and Index, QQQ, and the China JV led inflows, partly offset by Fundamental Equities outflows of $7.7B.
Investment management fees rose $360.9M y/y mainly on QQQ management fees after its conversion to an open-end ETF and higher average AUM, partly offset by lower service and distribution fees.
Expansion reflects operating income growing faster than revenue: a 70.0% y/y operating-income increase against a 20.5% revenue increase.
Net revenues grew $64.8M q/q while adjusted operating expenses rose only $2.1M, so nearly all incremental revenue converted to adjusted operating income -- the operating leverage management cited.
Revenue growth of $310.1M y/y outpaced a $160.1M rise in operating expenses, driven by higher third-party distribution costs and employee compensation tied to higher revenue.
Growth reflects the operating-income increase plus a $105.8M net gain on deferred-compensation and other investment market-value changes, partly offset by a $36.0M CIP-related expense.
The year-ago quarter included a $159.3M cost from repurchasing $1.0B of Series A Preferred Stock held by MassMutual; this quarter had no comparable charge, and pretax income nearly doubled.
Tracks the net-income swing described above; diluted share count was roughly flat versus both prior periods.
Adjusted net income rose 23.6% q/q on the same operating-leverage dynamics as adjusted operating income, with a modest tax-rate increase to 24.9% partly offsetting the gain.
Operating cash flow of $696.2M excluding CIP exceeded investing and financing outflows for buybacks and debt paydown, lifting the cash balance from $806.9M.
Debt fell to $1,624.0M as the credit-facility balance was paid down from $1,079.0M to $736.0M; combined with the higher cash balance this cut net debt by more than $450 million.

CEO Andrew Schlossberg called the momentum "noteworthy," citing record first-half net long-term inflows of $67B (7% annualized organic growth), 17% H1 net-revenue growth, and a sequential rise in adjusted EPS.
